gate: P (sunlight power, consistency and physical bounds)
proposed_by: Claude (backend session), 2026-11-13, after the team chose the power metric and before any real-data power output existed
approved_by: The team, 2026-11-13T10:02:13Z, before the first Gate P run
approval_rule: The team may change any number below before the first run of tools/power_check.py. After that run the numbers are frozen: a later change is a new gate, and the first result stays in validation/evidence/.
what_this_is_not: Not an independent validation. No published power or irradiance time series for these points is compared. The disc visibility it is built on passed Gate E (NASA Goddard PGDA 69 maps); this gate checks that the power layer is consistent with it and stays inside physical bounds on real data.
method_under_test: backend/lunar_core/power.py: E = 1361 W/m2 x (1 AU / r)^2 x visible disc fraction x cos(el) (vertical Sun-facing panel) or max(0, sin el) (flat panel), per 30 min step of the /api/compare run
derivation_of_bounds: Earth-Sun distance 0.98329-1.01671 AU, plus or minus the Moon's distance from Earth (at most 0.00272 AU): Moon-Sun 0.98057-1.01943 AU, so a full disc delivers 1361/1.01943^2 = 1309.6 to 1361/0.98057^2 = 1415.5 W/m2. The highest Sun elevation at latitude phi is (90 - |phi|) + 1.54 deg (lunar axial tilt to the ecliptic), so at 89 deg S or further south it is below 2.6 deg: cos(el) >= 0.998 and tan(el) <= 0.046.
verdict: PASS only if every criterion holds for every row of every request. A failure is recorded, not tuned.
